policy_title: Introduce Parental Controls for Social Media
stated: The Conservative Party will urgently consult on introducing further parental controls over children's access to social media, including effective age verification and necessary technology, building on the Online Safety Act.

source.quote: We will urgently consult on introducing further parental controls over access to social media. We know this is a complex area and we need more effective age verification and parental controls.

bearing_set.reason: Parental controls and age verification directly target children's online safety — reducing exposure to harmful content, grooming, and exploitation — which is a non-negligible safety intervention with contested efficacy.

Mandatory age verification requires collection of identity/biometric data (a real privacy trade-off), and access restrictions for minors raise genuine free-expression considerations under the strict O9 scope.
Uncontrolled children's social media use is linked to anxiety, depression and self-harm; effective parental controls plausibly move the mental-health-access indicator for young people.

Effective age verification requires platforms to collect and process identity data on all users, creating a privacy/surveillance mechanism; access restrictions for minors also constitute state-backed coercion over expression and online access — concrete O10 harms regardless of the safety intent.

membership_note: Classic O5/O10 tradeoff: the same age-verification mechanism that plausibly improves child safety (O5) materially worsens privacy and freedom from surveillance (O10). Other outcomes (O7 via educational wellbeing, O15 via cohesion) have only indirect or speculative mechanisms and do not clear the non-negligible bar.
